[Gazette of Punjab Extraordinary,
13th July, 2019]
No.
Legis: 13-33/2014(P-I), dated 13.7.2020.---The following Ordinance promulgated by Governor of the Punjab is
hereby published for general information:
It
is necessary to amend the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 (VII of 1925) for
the purposes hereinafter appearing.
Provincial
Assembly of the Punjab is not in session, and Governor of the Punjab is
satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary to take immediate
action.
In
exercise of the powers conferred under clause (1) of Article 128 of the
Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Governor of the Punjab is
pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance:
1. Short
title and commencement.---(1) This
Ordinance may be cited as the Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance,
2020.
(2) It
shall come into force at once.

11. Insertion
of section 17-C in Act VII of 1925.---In
the Act, after section 17-B, the following new section 17-C shall be inserted:
"17-C.
Transfer of interest in a housing society.- A member of a society shall cease to be the member of such society in
case all his interests in the immovable property in the society are transferred
in favour of any other person by sale, inheritance, gift or otherwise, and the
person acquiring such interests shall subject to the rules, be admitted as a
member:
Provided
that where more than one persons acquire the interests, one of such persons,
with mutual consent or the person older in age, shall be admitted as a member
having right to vote while other persons shall be the members without right to
vote:
Provided
further that where a minor or mentally disabled person acquires the interests,
the natural or legal guardian of the minor or, as the case may be, the person
bound to maintain the disabled person shall be admitted as a member and such
membership shall stand transferred to the minor as soon as he acquires majority
or to the disabled person as soon as his disability is removed.".

Grievance redressal.---(1) A member or a society can approach the Registrar
for redressal of grievances, not covered under section 54, by filing an
application.
(2) The
Registrar may issue notice to the parties, and after providing an opportunity
of hearing, redress the grievance through a written order.
(3) Any
party aggrieved by an order of the Registrar may file an appeal in the manner
as provided under section 64 of this Act, before the Secretary Cooperatives
within two months of the date of communication of the order.".

15. Amendment
of section 50-A of Act VII of 1925.---In
the Act, in section 50-A, for subsection (1), the following shall be
substituted:
"(1)
Where, in the course of winding up of a society, it appears that any person who
has taken part in the organization or management of the society or any past or
present Chairman, Secretary, member of managing committee or any officer of the
society has misapplied or retained or become liable or accountable for any
money or property of the society or has been guilty of misfeasance or breach of
trust in relation to the society or, where the society is acting under
subsection (4) of section 34 as agent of the financing bank, has made any
payment contrary to the instructions of the financing bank, the Registrar may
himself or on the recommendation of the liquidators, auditor, enquiry officer
in case of violation of section 44-D or any of the creditor or contributory of
such society, examine into the conduct of such person and make an order
requiring him to repay or restore the money or property or any part thereof
respectively with interest at such rate as the Registrar thinks just, or to
contribute such sum to the assets of the society or of the financing bank by
way of compensation in regard to the misapplication, retainer misfeasance or
breach of trust as the Registrar thinks just.".

penalty not exceeding rupees one million.
(2) The
Registrar or a person duly authorized by him shall be empowered to impose such
penalty after affording an opportunity of hearing to the concerned.".
